*What has been done:*

# Wrote down the functions for mm_saturation as well as the function a) based on steps and b) the derivative (made sure derivative is correct with WolframAlpha:
This is the derivative btw: (v=vmax,l=lambda,x=cost)

!Screenshot 2024-04-02 at 16.38.52.png|width=191,height=140,alt="Screenshot 2024-04-02 at 16.38.52.png"!

*NOTE:* if using the coefficient (transforming something to GMV) the derivative would be:

!Screenshot 2024-04-03 at 12.43.02.png|width=189,height=88,alt="Screenshot 2024-04-03 at 12.43.02.png"!
# Made sure that the functions work properly (used [this|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1_4Beh5XnWG-V_QZ23G-8k-m0i5uip-go3FTWTFDJK00/edit#gid=673704740] manual rebudgeting sheet to do manual checks)

# Checked how different the results would be if we used *25-step* vs *the derivative* with the assumption that vmax=lam (NOTE: if change the assumption, best re-evaluate the results)

# Derived the formula to get the spend given ROI threshold (aka derivative) validated it with manual data (see formula in further comment below) and validated it on manual data

# Compared the results provided by the derivative to the step results for real rebudgeting scenarios [here|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1_4Beh5XnWG-V_QZ23G-8k-m0i5uip-go3FTWTFDJK00/edit#gid=0]. Checking Aggressive and Passive scenarios did not give massive difference. Most often the difference is within 75 Eur
*Aggressive:*
!Aggressive scenario comparison.png|width=1564,height=654,alt="Aggressive scenario comparison.png"!
*Passive:*
!Passive scenario comparison.png|width=1564,height=654,alt="Passive scenario comparison.png"!


So the general result is:

* If either vmax is >100 or cost is >150Eur, the *difference between step function and derivative is not larger than 5-10%* (decreasing as either of vmax or cost grow)

!Screenshot 2024-04-03 at 18.08.45.png|width=1094,height=240,alt="Screenshot 2024-04-03 at 18.08.45.png"!

(table shows step_result/derivative for each combination of cost (column) and vmax (row)



*Suggested implications would be:*

* It seems that we are in general safe to use the derivative, because biggest difference happens at lower levels of spend, where we are more likely to neglect the difference (low volumes of spend + we cannot validate the impact at such small difference experimentally). 
* At higher levels I suggest to consider differences within 10% as negligible because our instruments do not measure the effectiveness as accurately.
* because we have larger amount of riders and often larger cost, I think this approach can be used for Rider already. 
* for driver it’s a bit more complicated. The thing is that we are not obtaining as many drivers, as riders (vmax is low) and the spend is often also lower (low cost), so in this case:

Let’s start with some context first. Debt relations checks were introduced due to exactly the behaviour you have described. [~accountid:712020:5382507a-151c-4326-b1f8-6a2d888c30bb] we should of course not communicate this to the drivers or riders, but:

* Having stickers would tick one of the boxes when it comes to compliance with privacy laws (the obligation to inform about video recording)
* There are other obligations under privacy laws that need to be fulfilled for the filming to be compliant
* Having a sticker by itself does not make the recording legal; on the other hand - no sticker does not mean that the recording is non-compliant.
* Generally, a sticker would be considered a better way to inform the passenger vs. informing the passenger orally. Again, this is not something we should tell the drivers at this point. 

*Why am I asking to not tell this to the drivers:*

* Bolt is not in a position to issue legal advice to the drivers
* Us saying that something is compliant or not will bring us certain implications. Since we do not initiate the CCTV recordings ourselves, we do not have the relevant procedures/policies in place to facilitate this. GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7

orders AS (

a.city_id

--	WHEN a.name IN ('CS_RIDES_RIDE_DID_NOT_HAPPENED','CS_RIDES_SHORT_PICKUP','CS_RIDES_SUSPICIOUS_DRIVER') AND json_array_contains(a.issue_keys,'rider_did_not_pay') THEN 1

ran the above query for Dec/23, Jan/24, Feb/24 and Mar/24

it’s around 50k euros per month. however, this is a very rough number that shouldn’t be taken too seriously tbh. in Rides, the biggest fraud abuse happens on the driver side, and we don’t have data on manual CS compensations to drivers. the number provided by the query is just cases we’ve denied automated refunds for riders and a refund still happened, which also doesn’t mean the refund was poorly executed by agents. the driver abuse should be many times bigger than the one from riders. 

from Rides' perspective, the value that we can assure we’ll get will be from other use cases. I’ll illustrate three to give you an idea:

* driver fraud with toll abuse
** [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05LLPT628N/p1710845809309659|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05LLPT628N/p1710845809309659|smart-link] 
** drivers in UK are heavily abusing riders by just driving through airport tolls. the rider gets a massive overcharge, complains to CS and often gets a full refund done by the automation that does it with the actor at fault being Bolt. that means that the refund doesn’t affect driver’s balance. they keep the money. rider get a free ride and driver makes a profit by doing fraud. we tried a product approach to solve it, but drivers adapted. a proper solution would be possible with partial refunds to the user’s payment method and with integration of Fraud and Beehive. for these abusive drivers, we would reject automated compensations and trigger a message in Beehive to make it clear that the driver is doing fraud to make sure that CS refunds with driver at fault, to deduct the money from their balances. that’s how the scheme dies down. as of now, we’re losing 1k euros per day on this. so this single use-case would add 30k euros per month value. 
!Screenshot 2024-04-02 at 14.52.25.png|width=1056,height=877,alt="Screenshot 2024-04-02 at 14.52.25.png"!
* rides automatically recalculated by Fraud
** Fraud has the ability to recalculate rides at their end. when that happens, the info is displayed on admin, but it’s often not perceived by agents. this [order|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/498559089/853603637] for example. Fraud pushed the price back to the upfront. in the Price section in the admin-panel you can see that there was an overcharge correction action by fraud. we could benefit from building a rule on our engine and displaying that info for CS on Beehive. this way, CS doesn’t go ahead and compensate the driver thinking that there was a pricing calculation issue. with a message on beehive, we can avoid excessive overrule decisions of fraud actions. 
!Screenshot 2024-04-02 at 14.49.18.png|width=621,height=354,alt="Screenshot 2024-04-02 at 14.49.18.png"!

* resellers (groups on telegram, whatsapp that resell orders on Bolt for cheap)
** we constantly are fighting resellers. these are guys that either use stolen cards or know how to force failed payments in our platform. they then sell orders on Bolt with a big discount. 50% for example. we’re constantly battling them, rejecting their orders. once, they were running out of options so they appealed to social engineering. they were doing rides with 2, 3 stops intentionally when the rider’s destination was at the 1st stop. then they would reach support and demand a full refund because the order was unfinished. with integration with Beehive, we could highlight these orders to instruct CS to never give full refunds and only partials. 

these are only three examples where we would get a lot of value by integrating Fraud with Beehive. the scenarios are endless. once dev work is done, we could use this endpoint to communicate quickly with CS for any sort of fraud scenario.

Test yaml. Make sure that {{serviceAccountName}} is specifiead and the service account has IAM role with access to the S3 bucket that stores admin-panel assets.

Command is intentionally complex as uploading admin-panel module is a process that consists of multiple operations:

# upload module
# activate module

Also, if module is {{app}}, commands to activate and upload differ (activate-app & upload-app instead of activate-module & upload-module).

Module activation:

{noformat}apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: admin-panel_general-reporting-framework
  namespace: builder
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: builder-access
      containers:
      - name: admin-panel-cli
        image: registry-dev.taxify.io/taxify-webapp-admin-panel/prelive-generalreportingframework:20240404-0930-784a03a
        env:
          - name: AWS_BUCKET_NAME
            value: bolt-prelive-builder-static-web-apps
        command: ["/bin/sh"]
        args:
          - -c
          -
            echo "Uploading module";
            node /app/framework/scripts/lattice-cli upload-module -m general-reporting-framework -f admin-panel.test.bolt.eu;
            echo "Activating module";
            node /app/framework/scripts/lattice-cli activate-module -m general-reporting-framework -f admin-panel.test.bolt.eu -t 5.1701.0;
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 1{noformat}

Module removal:

{noformat}apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: admin-panel_general-reporting-framework
  namespace: builder
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: builder-access
      containers:
      - name: admin-panel-cli
        image: registry-dev.taxify.io/taxify-webapp-admin-panel/prelive-generalreportingframework:20240404-0930-784a03a
        env:
          - name: AWS_BUCKET_NAME
            value: bolt-prelive-builder-static-web-apps
        command: ["/bin/sh"]
        args:
          - -c
          -
            echo "Deleting module";
            node /app/framework/scripts/lattice-cli activate-module -m general-reporting-framework -f admin-panel.test.bolt.eu -t delete;
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 1{noformat}

{noformat}with summary as (
select 
asc2.country_code,
order_id,
sum(case when subtype like '%dropoff%' then 1 else 0 end) as dropoff_count,
sum(case when subtype like '%dropoff%' then sum_with_vat/cer.rate else 0 end) as dropoff_sum_eur,
sum(case when subtype like '%pickup%' then 1 else 0 end) as pickup_count,
sum(case when subtype like '%pickup%' then sum_with_vat/cer.rate else 0 end) as pickup_sum_eur
from ng_delivery.delivery_invoicing_record dir
left join ng_public.admin_system_city asc2 on asc2.id = dir.city_id
left join ng_public.currency_exchange_rates cer on cer.currency = dir.currency and cer.valid_on = dir.created_date
where created_date >= DATE('2023-04-01') and created_date < DATE('2024-04-01')
and type = 'cashPayment'
and subtype != 'takeaway'
group by 1,2
)
select 
country_code,
--sum(dropoff_count) as eater_paid_count,
sum(dropoff_sum_eur) as eater_paid_sum_eur,
--sum(pickup_count) as courier_paid_count,
sum(pickup_sum_eur) as courier_paid_sum_eur,
count(*) as total_orders,
count(case when dropoff_count >= 1 and pickup_count = 0 then order_id else null end) as eater_paid_order_count,
count(case when pickup_count >= 1 and dropoff_count = 0 then order_id else null end) as courier_paid_order_count,
count(case when pickup_count >= 1 and dropoff_count >= 0 then order_id else null end) as both_paid_order_count
from summary
group by 1{noformat}

Hi Marija,


The user is seeing a block message not because of the negative balance but because of the many failed card-adding attempts within a short period of time. As mentioned, the initial fraud decision for the card-adding attempts was “pass,” indicating that there were no restrictions from the fraud side during the first attempts. However, the bank declined these attempts. We have fraud rules in place for card-adding velocity checks. This means that if a user has more than X failed card-adding attempts within a certain period (which can be daily, weekly, or monthly), they exceed the threshold and receive a “reject” decision from the fraud system, resulting in a block message. 


In conclusion, the user should first contact the bank to address the issues with card-adding declines to avoid triggering our velocity rules and getting the block message.
Regarding recovering the negative balance, I see that the user has tried to top up their balance with an existing card and was successful.


Also, please refrain from providing detailed information to this user, as their profile indicates suspicious activity with card-adding attempts from different countries. The user had more than 50 card-adding attempts with 9 different card countries. Furthermore, the user is not passing our 3DS challenge request, which is another indication of fraudulent behaviour.


Best,

Generally robberies both driver and rider fall in two categories:

1. Non violent.
2. Violent.

*1*.*Rider robbed or attempted to rob the Driver*

Non violent robbery include;

* Stealing 
* Snatching.

*Violent.*

In this case:

* A weapon is used e.g gun or knife. 
* Sometimes the driver/ rider is injured.
* Police are involved.


*2. Driver Robbed or Attempted to Rob Rider*  

Non violent robbery include;

* Stealing - When the client claims to have left the car and their belongings to get checked at a check point then upon arrival to the destination he or she noticed missing items and claims to have found the bag open. (They usually swear they had confirmed the items while entering the car)
*  Delivery - When a driver accepts a regular trip to deliver an item (trip not ordered through Bolt send) then cancels the trip and takes off with the item. 
* During a stop over when the customer takes too long then the driver decides to take off with the clients items in the car.
* Snatching, when a driver snatches the rider’s phone at the pickup point.
* Payment issues where the driver takes a client’s item and holds the item hostage until the rider makes payment.

*Violent.*

Hey [~accountid:62bbfa39ec4c0d377f9fc3b7] 
I have to make a small correction regarding my assessment. The provisions references by Thomas are not under the chapter which is not applicable to Bolt Norway Drivers (and they therefore apply). This however still doesn't result in a need to amend the T&Cs (mainly because the other provisions regarding maximum prices and allowed surcharges are still NOT applicable).

One relevant provision that essentially IS applicable is the second paragraph of [§ 3 of maksprisforskriften|https://lovdata.no/forskrift/2010-09-30-1307/§3] which states: "_The customer must pay what gives the lowest total price for the trip from any price offer, a fixed price that may be offered for the route and the parallel fare with any supplements._" This means that if the Upfront Fare offered to Passengers would be regarded as either "price offer" or "fixed price" then, in case Upfront Fare is offered, the referenced provision must be followed (i.e., the Passenger must be charged whichever is lower: either the Upfront Fare or regular fare). In this case, a T&C amendment might also be necessary, namely [clause 3.6 in the Passenger T&C|https://bolt.eu/no-no/legal/tnc-rider/?category=rides#:~:text=3.6.%20Advance%20price,route%20with%20tolls).] with adding an additional reason for when the Upfront Fare will not be applied (something along the lines of “_when the regular trip fee with all surcharges will be lower than the Upfront Fare_”).

However, my assessment is that both the "price offer" and "fixed price" are not used by Drivers, i.e., the Upfront Fare does not meet the definitions of either of them.


* "Price offer" is defined in a [separate regulation|https://lovdata.no/forskrift/2012-11-14-1066/§12] and its key element is that it is a price offer made at the _request of the consumer_ - by my understanding, Upfront Fare can only be offered by the Driver and it +cannot+ be requested by the Passenger - *is this correct?*

* "Fixed price" is defined as a pre-determined price for a given route (an example is given here: Oslo Airport to Oslo city center). As I understand it, the "fixed price" would apply if Bolt had a list of pre-determined routes with pre-determined prices - but this is not the case.

Therefore, the Upfront Fare does not meet the definition either and when it is offered to Passengers, the referenced provision does not need to be followed (i.e., the Passenger doesn’t have to be charged whichever price is lowest).

_The public administrations, as well as any natural or legal person, shall provide the judicial authorities, the Public Prosecutor's Office or the Judicial Police with the data, reports, background information and supporting documents requested by them and which are necessary for the investigation and prosecution of criminal offences or for the enforcement of penalties.   ROUND((SUM (ROUND(etl.chargeback_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate,2)) - (sum(CASE WHEN etl.card_scheme = 'mastercard' AND etl.card_country IN ('at','be', 'bg', 'hr', 'cz', 'cy', 'dk','ee','fi','fr', 'de', 'gr', 'hu', 'ie', 'it','lt','lv'

Based on what I read from this thread, I assume there is also a simultaneous conversation happening separately with BCG in email. It seems that I’m not included in this email conversation. 

In order to provide my best input here, would be great if you could forward the email exchange to me, so I would have more visibility on what kind of response exactly is needed 🙏 



However, coming into this conversation with half the context, I can provide you with the following draft. Kindly let me know if, considering the context, this response is not accurate or needs to be adjusted. 

As of my current knowledge, the following covers are required by BCG (please correct me if I’m wrong) 

*(i) - Commercial General Liability*

Bolt has some local policies, bought only where this has been required by the regulatory authorities. Aon has provided a quote for a global GL policy in the past, however Bolt chose not to buy this (due to cost). In conclusion, Bolt can buy this policy, if willing to pay the cost. 

*(ii) - Workers’ Compensation*

Bolt does not have such cover. This insurance product is not available in Europe (this is US specific policy). 

*(iii) - Employer’s Liability* 

Bolt has bought this cover in some countries but don’t have global policy. 

It is possible to buy this coverage globally, but this will come with certain caveats: with Bolt Operations OÜ as the policyholder, the territorial validity can be the whole word, however the applicable jurisdiction will be Estonian, which means that Estonian legislation is the basis for settling the employer's liability insurance claim. 

*(iV) - Business Automobile Liability*

This is something that Bolt does not currently buy. Bolt has a Motor Contingent placed in the UK. However, Business Automobile Liability as such is not possible to place as a pan-European policy - the legislation varies from country to country. For most cases, this can be bought to top-up cover for MTPL (e.g. where the MTPL limit has been exhausted). 

The EU operates very differently from the U.S., as EU countries have the 4th EU Motoring Directive which means all member countries must have a provision for uninsured vehicles. Also, the insurance for ride-hailing vehicles is the responsibility of the vehicle owner and not the operator, unlike in the U.S. Therefore, the need to have a non-owned auto/motor insurance policy is not that common in the EU. 

*(V) Professional Indemnity Insurance*

Bolt does not have this coverage, and it’s really not possible to place this cover for Bolt. The main issue being that Bolt does not provide professional services.  

*(vi)* *Property Damage*

Property insurance is of course available - locations and list of insured property is needed. Care, Custody and Control extension can be added to GL policy (which we don’t currently buy see (I), if needed, but risk must be identified – what kind of third-party property could be in Bolt’s Care, Custody and Control and what could be the value of this property/limit of liability.



Best regards

Karmel

hey [~accountid:6389e5ac5fce844d606c13ed],

Below are the recommendations for the research stage of this project. Assessment of this system for further deployment to live chat data should be assessed separately based on the research results.


1. *Lawfulness of using user’s data for this project:*

The mere chat functionality is created to facilitate the comms between the driver and the rider during the active order. However, the chat data is also collected and stored by Bolt for investigating and detecting fraudulent payments, malicious or unlawful activities, and/or safety or security incidents, maintaining the safety of the platform, and responding to suspected or actual criminal acts. 

As this research stage and further implementation is aimed to detect abusive behaviour of users while communicating with each other and improve Bolt platform safety for its users, we consider that the initial goal of collecting and storing this chat data aligns with the purpose of using this chat data for research purposes. The detailed privacy analysis of this conclusion can be found [*here*|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1toEMyjNRfMt6pNwzQi7FrMtejPnG4zCoWj0-XoAXJEU/edit]*.* 

*Recommendations for the stakeholders for the Research Stage:*

# *Striving to anonymisation.* As was discussed previously, *we ask you to provide as little identifiable information as possible.* We appreciate that we cannot clean up the chat information that was input by the users voluntarily as this information can be helpful for the research. Bolt does not anticipate any special categories of data (health data, sex life data, political opinion data, etc) to be a part of the chats, but we recognise that sensitive data like financial data can be a part of the research.
# *Verifying final results*. Please note that this is one of the key parts of this system to be further deployed. When you test the data and receive initial results, you need to check whether the received information is not biased, non-discriminative and not false-positive.
## There are no clear rules to apply for bias, but when you verify the data you have to check cultural norms and morals of the case being considered abusive. 
## We recommend having clear instructions for people who would check initial results and decide on re-testing: how accuracy is measured, whether there is a need for additional data, for example to improve accuracy or to eliminate bias, what would need to be re-tested, what would need to be escalated to respective teams, etc. Ensure that we have a representation of people from diverse backgrounds and cultures to ensure diversity of opinions on the results.
## Moreover, all the results of the verification in case you believe the system provided inappropriate results, must be documented , including measures you took to improve this (like enhancing human control of the final results for deployment stage or not using AI for these cases). 
## Also, we have to ensure that people who verify the system's initial results for bias, discrimination, and false-positives do not take the results as true ones because it’s an AI who may know better, e.g. we have to apply our human cognitive ability with due care.

All of the above is necessary for further implementation and documentation of how the system was tested and how we ensured it does not provide inaccurate results.

# *Notice to users in the app:* No clear notice to users will be made for *the research stage* only as the mere research can be considered a compatible purpose (see the analysis in Privacy Review for Research stage section), it’s temporary and does not pose a medium or high risk for users: we do not block users, we would provide as little as possible identifiable information of users to the LLM system. 
# *Comprehensive data used for AI training.* I appreciate we do not train the system and use the product from the shelf. We would ask you to ensure that training data have enough representation from different countries and cultural norms. It means that we should ensure that we can apply this system for all countries because the system is trained enough on what is hate speech or harassment in some countries.
## If we take the position that we apply a world-approach to abusive behaviour, we should ensure we test it in different countries, eg I would recommend reverting back to global testing, but minimising the amount of messages for the first testing. Here is the clash btw privacy requirement to use as minimal data as possible and AI-development approach to comprehensive data. From my side, provided that we are going to launch this system further and some users can be blocked due to the results, we can find a balance and test it globally, but reduce the amount of messages.
# *Retention period of this data should be as we agreed:* 6 months after the initial testing is completed. The purpose for keeping this data for 6 months is to decide on re-testing of data and analyse results before deploying the project. Further use of this data (block users, etc) is not allowed. 
## We would appreciate if you set the process of automatically deleting this data after 6 months, eg no human error happen.
# *Access rights to results.* Please limit the number of people who can access users’ data, and under what circumstances, including an oversight mechanism to log when, where, how, by whom and for what purpose data was accessed.

Please let me know if anything from the above is not relevant. 

Also, I would recommend asking the legal team checking whether the agreement with OpenAI does not prohibit us from using their system for this testing. As we concluded the agreement for CS chat support, there can be limitations on further use of their system for other purposes. Just fyi.

Another question that we frequently receive is whether the training material and a test should be sent to the courier before enabling alcohol deliveries. 

In Lithuania, we have the following practices:

* When the courier leads fill out the form to start working as Bolt’s courier, they receive training material on both the cash and alcohol deliveries.

Hi [~accountid:5d723b3830f82c0c36be5b56], thanks for the great questions.



*Effects on the rider account*

* _“If they do this, we cannot refund the order back to their original payment method anymore. Instead, the refund will go to their Bolt Balance”_ means:
** Rider had failed payment that became a negative Bolt Balance
** Rider added money to their Bolt Balance to clear the debt
** Rider is asking for a refund for *that ride* (for which the payment was failed)
** It’s not possible to refund to the original payment method, the *refund can only be done to Bolt Balance*. 
* So only the refund for that particular ride is affected. But thank you for flagging that this note is unclear, we will edit it. 



*Unpaid cash rides*

* _“Educate the rider based on the situation”_ means that the agent has to educate the rider based on why the rider didn't pay in cash, e.g. they forgot or didn’t know how to change the payment method.
* _“When the rider is not blocked, why we do not explain in KB when the riders account will result in suspension”_ → We don’t disclose exact blocking rules to riders to avoid giving the rider the possibility not to pay if they don’t mind being blocked, e.g. the rider would be blocked for 7 days if they don’t pay twice, so if the rider would know this, they can simply not pay if they don’t mind not using Bolt for 7 days. However, agents know the blocking rules as they are documented [here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360015016234]. 
* _“How the Rider can pay for the unpaid cash trip”_ → They can’t. We analyzed this topic with the CXA team and decided that riders shouldn’t pay for their unpaid rides, because:
** We can’t track payments made outside the app.
** To pay, the rider needs to get the driver’s bank account and/or phone number. Sharing personal details poses a risk of GDPR violation.
** Involving CS as a middleman in such transactions creates complexity, as CS don’t have control over them and can end up in situations where they can’t provide any help.
** Payments outside the app prolong the resolution process, requiring extensive follow-up by CS until both parties confirm payment settlement.
** The driver receives compensation either through automation or manually by CS.
** The rider eventually gets blocked, as not paying for rides violates our rules and we don’t want to allow such riders to continue doing so.

“app” module activation and removal:

Required input:

* app name and module name (to compose job k8s job name, must not exceed 63 characters length)
* AWS_BUCKET_NAME
* image
* environment (to identify domain)
* app version

Example (runs on prelive-euc-1-alpha-test):

{noformat}apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: admin-panel_app
  namespace: builder
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: builder-access
      containers:
      - name: admin-panel-cli
        image: registry-dev.taxify.io/taxify-webapp-admin-panel/prelive-app:20240404-0930-784a03a
        env:
          - name: AWS_BUCKET_NAME
            value: bolt-prelive-builder-static-web-apps
        command: ["/bin/sh"]
        args:
          - -c
          -
            echo "Uploading app";
            node /app/framework/scripts/lattice-cli upload-app -f admin-panel.test.bolt.eu;
            echo "Activating app";
            node /app/framework/scripts/lattice-cli activate-app -f admin-panel.test.bolt.eu -t 5.1701.0;
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 1{noformat}

[AUTO_INCREMENT|https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/auto-increment] - the next value when any insert on the table will be (for AUTO_INCREMENT column)
[AUTO_ID_CACHE|https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/auto-increment#cache-size-control] - how to control the amount of  AUTO_INCREMENT values that each TiDB node will have assigned to it.

{quote}Instance {{A}} might cache the auto-increment IDs of {{[1,30000]}}, and instance {{B}} might cache the auto-increment IDs of {{[30001,60000]}}. In {{INSERT}} statements to be executed, these cached IDs of each instance will be assigned to the {{AUTO_INCREMENT}} column as the default values.{quote}

# In general, we have drawn the process for handling law enforcement requests for a dual reason - to assist the police as fast as possible and to stay in line with the requirements of privacy laws, such as the GDPR.
# In short, when we receive a request from the police to disclose personal data to them, we need to assess the validity and proportionality of this request. While we do not dig too deep into the crime itself, we need to assess whether the police is acting in a proportional manner, for example, that they don’t ask 5 years worth of order history to investigate a littering case.
# Perhaps it would be best to explain to the police *why we are doing this:*
## in order to not breach the EU GDPR, which is a directly applicable law and is not below the local laws, we need to evaluate whether the requested data is proportionate (Article 5 of the GDPR).
## in order to stay in line with the requirements of Articles 5 and 6 of the GDPR, we need to have a legal basis to share the data. Therefore, we always request the police the provide a reference to a specific law that sets the right of the police to request personal data from a company such as Bolt.

Hi All, just to recap our discussion here:

* We are being intimated by Police to enter into a partnership with a local security service provider appointed by them. Officially, there are no consequences for refusing, but it will apparently result in bad PR and more intimidation from the Police. Thus, we don’t really have a choice but to proceed with a partnership with the appointed service provider by the Police in PY. 
* We are going to do a ‘Test’ with service providers who will provide CCTV and panic button services — 50 cameras in-vehicle to start. We will be paying for this Test.
* If the Test is successful, the service provider will be redirected to engage directly with drivers who can sign agreements with the service provider for the CCTV, subsidised by Bolt.
* Technically, the service provider will store CCTV recordings in their cloud and Drivers will by default have access to those recordings for 90 days.

From a Privacy-Legal perspective, it is positive that Bolt will not be entering into a contract for the service provider to provide CCTV and panic button services to Drivers (the contractual relationship will be directly between Drivers and the Service Provider). This limits our risk somewhat. However, Bolt nevertheless has quite a bit of influence over the way that this initiative would be rolled out and should (informally) propose ways in which privacy of our Users can be protected (by the service provider).

My recommendations to [~accountid:6267f69e494f17007055df5c] and [~accountid:638e1e5f9960988ef6c1ec87] / [~accountid:6149a0e9ba1b34006ab04897] were as follows:

# Bring this forced partnership to [~accountid:60bd1ba800bdd900683be5fd] 's attention please. While PY is a special case, it is important he is aware of what is being considered here.
# *Limit retention period*: we should propose to the Police/service provider that CCTV recordings are only kept for 7-14 days as opposed to 90 days, which should be enough time for them to be accessed for criminal proceedings.
# *Limit access to CCTV recordings*: we should propose that the Police/service provider only grant access to a CCTV recording if the person making the requests was the Driver or Passenger in the trip and has formally lodged a claim/charge with the Police. This way, the Service Provider can minimise the changes of CCTV recordings being used for other purposes.
# *Include a limitation of liability & Indemnity clause in the contract for the Test with the Service Provider*: [~accountid:6149a0e9ba1b34006ab04897] - we should limit our liability during the Test and anytime after that. I can help with the wording if you need.
# *Transparency & Notification*: Drivers should ideally put up signs in their vehicles that they have CCTV cameras so that Passengers are aware. We can’t force this though, as we are not the one’s making the recordings or managing the recordings.

h3. *AHT observations*

* _January 2024_ - {color:#bf2600}*6.8 min* {color}(168 tickets)
* _February 2024_ - {color:#bf2600}*6.8 min* {color}(182 tickets)

🗺️ [*AHT outlier countries*|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/explore/support/support_data?qid=UGWZtnwTkEptCZhsuVrREx&origin_space=1301&toggle=dat,vis]*:*

* Positive outliers - *Lithuania* ({color:#006644}*5.7 min for 82 tickets*{color}), *Portugal* ({color:#006644}*4.5 min for 53 tickets*{color})
* Negative outliers - *Latvia* ({color:#bf2600}*9.1 min for 49 tickets*{color}), *Sweden* ({color:#bf2600}*7.2 min for 36 tickets*{color}).


🎫 [*Ticket deep dive*|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/explore/support/support_data?qid=ilHvuOfGTenfoFziAYvLMS&origin_space=1301&toggle=dat,vis]*:*

[Deep dive observations|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1HPogZxo8a0Jb1aGHg3XQF-htAHE710xLDmvKA-1lAeo/edit#gid=1577592097] of the top 40 tickets with the highest AHT:

* Almost half of the tickets are incorrectly tagged (19) - this issue tag gets confused with *_I want to reconcile the debt_*, *_I have sent my debt payment_* and invoice-related issue tags.
* In 5 tickets this issue tag should have been used alongside other issue tags, most commonly with *_I want to reconcile the debt_*.
* Based on the ticket deep dive and the descriptions of tags from the [💼 Business Company issues list|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/87371] article, these are the potential reasons for using the following issue tags:
** *_I have a question about debt_* - BA asking about existing debt, where it's from, the current state of the company balance, or reporting difficulties while paying for the debt;
** *_I want to reconcile the debt_* - BA asking for Bolt's credentials to pay for the debt, informing that they'd like to pay for the debt and asking how to do it, general questions about the debt and how billing works;
** *_I have sent my debt payment_* - BA informing us that they have paid for the debt, payment matching process.

----

h3. [*CSAT/DSAT observations*|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/explore/support/support_data?qid=eTedBXBQoFEBr37DOfPr2V&origin_space=1301&toggle=fil,vis]

* _March 2024_ - {color:#006644}*100%*{color}{color:#bf2600} {color}(4 feedbacks)

----

h3. *Results of pre-analysis*

* The separation of the debt-related issue tags is too granular - the CS team does not have a clear idea about when this issue tag should be used, it gets confused with other debt-related issue tags, thus incorrectly used.
* *_I want to reconcile the debt_* does not necessarily match the[ 💼 Business Administrator sends their debt payment|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/11151962740370] process.

----

h3. 🎯 *Action plan*

# Reach out to CXA for the context on why the issue tags are so detailed and limited.
# Report the incorrect issue tagging to Quality.
# Create a separate process for *_I want to reconcile the debt_* issue tag.

It works both in Spark and Presto using the single schema, because you write using the plain Parquet format. It is readable by both tools with no problems. In this case, you can simply write to the non-spark schema.   

It would be a different case if you wanted to write in the Delta Lake format. Delta Lake is more powerful than Parquet, but it is not directly readable by Presto, so it would need this schema duality. A tool to help write in Delta Lake from Python is [https://github.com/bolteu/dataeng-pyspark-jobs/tree/main/bolt_delta_lake|https://github.com/bolteu/dataeng-pyspark-jobs/tree/main/bolt_delta_lake|smart-link]

As i mentioned, apparently Sweden is a market where wait time is widely spread and a normal thing to have in the orders, seen by the big volumes. But opposite that, the bad orders volume (or the reported ones) which we would consider fraud in the paid wait time scenarios is very small. Above are the stats for period of 2 months. And it has to be considered that some of the payments turning bad or users reports can also be for other reasons, but for simplicity here i have taken all bad orders. 
If we do not see reports or bad orders, we from fraud side can’t react or justify a decision if it doesn’t have impact or fraud justification. 
Same would be in the 26 March examples you sent for the overcharged orders, only 4 have been reported. We can’t justify action just because an order looks weird or suspicious, we need to make data driven decision from fraud side. 
If the local team decision is to target all orders under certain conditions, regardless of the fraud rate, than a solution would need be found on product side as a feature or restriction, rather than on fraud side. 

Anyways, i have two suggestion on this, because we are not going to leave it un-attended. 

For the overcharge “not finished correctly” orders i ran numbers on the entire market and i found some patterns which i will turn into rule today, which in the abusing scenario turn a recalculation logic and price will be reverted to upfront so the overcharge part doesn’t happen.

Why the refund is done with actor at fault: bolt?

I would advice an instruction to agents that handle the Swedish market, to change this flow, when driver is at fault and overcharge happens, to refund with actor at fault: driver. Otherwise whatever we do is going to be pointless.

Hi! We received quite a detailed response on the simple question of which VAT rate:

According to the Tax Administration’s (FTA) guidelines, if another company handles the delivery process e.g. on behalf of a store, the delivery is subject to the general VAT rate of 24%. It is noted in the FTA’s guidelines, that the general VAT rate is also applied if a restaurant or store purchases the delivery service from a subcontractor. In our understanding, *the standard VAT rate of 24% is applicable to the contemplated package deliveries.*

We understand that the packages may contain all kinds of products and are not limited to e.g. restaurant meals or groceries. Further, we understand that Bolt does not intend to establish stores from which the products will be sold, but simply start a package delivery platform. +However, we’d like to point out that it is mentioned in the FTA’s guidelines that if a restaurant or store handles the home delivery by itself, the tax rate applied to the meals or groceries (14%) is also applied to the delivery.+ Also, if the staff of a grocery store collects and packages the products that the customer has ordered in boxes or bags for the customer to pick up or delivers the products to the customer’s home, both the pick up service and home delivery are subject to the current reduced VAT rate of 14%. Grocery stores also often sell other products besides groceries, and these are subject to another VAT rate. For example, cleaning products are subject to 24% VAT. If the customer’s order includes these products, the tax rate for the pickup service and home delivery is determined in proportion to the tax rates of the different products the customer has ordered.

There are not any particular tax considerations to be taken into account in case the client who wants to have a package delivered is a business client. VAT-registered business clients who have incurred the costs in the course their own business purposes can deduct the VAT.

As a market comment, we’d like to point out that it seems that Wolt has deviated from the above-described VAT treatment in their restaurant meal and other deliveries (e.g. deliveries from grocery stores and other shops). It seems that Wolt has applied the reduced rate of 14% to the grocery store deliveries and restaurant deliveries instead of the standard 24% rate. This practice deviates from the published guidelines of the FTA.

+*Reclassification risks*+: {color:#ff5630}MEDIUM TO HIGH{color}

* As anticipated, they agree with me that offering this EV Project to *Fleet Owners only* (_and not to independent / private drivers_) *will significantly lower the risk of reclassification*.
* However, *even if this offer is limited to Fleet Owners* (FOs), *the reclassification risks would remain medium to high*.
* Their +recommendations+ are therefore as follows:
** *Only include FOs*, ie a B2B partnership (not private drivers;
** *Send the offer to all FOs and not by priority to the trusted FOs* (who already perform their services mainly for Bolt). 
** *Reduce the duration of the contract to* *12 months renewable*
** *Provide the possibility to freely negotiate certain clauses* (e.g. monthly KPI's, exclusivity, etc.). 
** *Mitigate the reasons to terminate the contract for gross misconduct* (could be perceived as a sanction) - _Nb: I am clarifying this with OC and asking them for examples/wording_

+*Risk of unauthorized advertising*+: {color:#ff5630}MEDIUM TO HIGH{color}

* As for the other branded cars in BE, for this project the sticker with the *legal disclaimer "**_non-exclusive affiliation with the Bolt booking intermediary_**" needs to be affixed* on all cars.
* *However this does not completely protect Bolt* from the risks of unauthorized advertising. 
* *The green colour all over the cars could be seen as unnecessary to simply inform about the affiliation to Bolt and therefore increases the risk that it will be considered as advertising even with the disclaimer*.
* +Potential consequences+:
** Brussels Mobility could prohibit Bolt from using advertising signs and green colour.;
** Being in breach of the Brussels Taxi Regulation can constitute an *offense punishable by a prison sentence* (between 8 days and 3 months) - _for the (identifiable) manager(s) if it is evidenced that the manager(s) was behind the idea leading to the practice and proceeded with knowledge -_ and/or a *fine of up to €80K* _- possibly €160K if jail time is converted in fine_;
** Competitors could launch a cease-and-desist action in order to obtain an injunction to cease the use of all the advertising signs.

+*Risk of Greenwashing & misleading commercial practice*+*:* {color:#ff5630}MEDIUM TO HIGH{color}

* The colour green is linked to ecology and is used by some industries to participate in greenwashing strategies.
* It is therefore *not recommended to invoke the fact that the colour green is linked to ecology as it could potentially lead to accusations of greenwashing and be considered as misleading commercial practice*. 
* +Potential consequences+:
** The regulator could request us to modify or remove the advertisement deemed misleading or false.  
** This could also lead to a *legal cease-and-desist action* brought by the Minister of Economy or a competitor.
** The Minister of Economy has also the authority to investigate and impose a Level 2 fine which consists of a *criminal fine* (max €80K or 4% of the total annual sales turnover).

+*Contract*+:

* *The existence of a contract between Bolt and the FO may increase the risk of unauthorized advertising*. 
* We could envisage a branding contract, ideally based upon the current branding terms, however this approach carries a risk due to the subtle distinction between branding and advertising, which can be tight in practice.

{color:#0747a6}+*Conclusion*+{color}{color:#0747a6}:{color}

Hi [~accountid:5f689921f0d401007029c6b0], 

We looked into this and found that [+maksprisforskriften+|https://lovdata.no/dokument/SF/forskrift/2010-09-30-1307] does apply to Drivers because the terms between Drivers and Passengers are not negotiated.

While the Drivers are compliant with the parallel tariff requirement (i.e., “paralleltakst”), the Drivers are currently _not compliant_ with charging Passengers the lowest of any price offer or parallel tariff ([+second paragraph of § 3 of maksprisforskriften+|https://lovdata.no/dokument/SF/forskrift/2010-09-30-1307#:~:text=Kunden%20skal%20betale%20det%20som%20gir%20den%20laveste%20totalprisen%20for%20turen%20av%20et%20eventuelt%20pristilbud%2C%20en%20fastpris%20som%20eventuelt%20tilbys%20p%C3%A5%20strekningen%20og%20parallelltaksten%20med%20eventuelle%20tillegg.], also Passengers must be notified of the existence of this requirement).

It is important to note that Drivers are obligated to provide a price offer in all cases – this stems from a separate price information regulation (namely [+§ 25d+|https://lovdata.no/forskrift/2012-11-14-1066/%C2%A725d] of said regulation). The price estimation given in the Bolt app can be classified as a price offer – therefore this requirement is complied with. However, while in many cases the price estimation corresponds to the actual fare charged from the Passenger, this may not always be the case as the final fare may change as a result of the trip getting longer or additional fees being added. In such a case, the Passenger is not charged the price estimation but the actual time/distance fare (or the “paralleltakst”). If the actual time/distance fare were to be higher than the initial price estimation, then, according to the maksprisforskriften, the Passenger must be charged the price estimation as it is the lowest of the two.

This practice is currently not followed by Bolt when acting on the Drivers’ behalf and therefore the Drivers are essentially not compliant with the law.

As a next step, can you please explain how many trips end up being higher than the initial price estimation? This will allow us to assess the potential extent of non-compliance and let business decide on next steps.

Best regards,

Dan

Hey folks, for some reason, the content of the ticket got lost, so I am better resending the query. 

In CS, we have an issue tag called 'My account has been blocked unfairly,' which implies that the driver disagrees with their account being blocked and wants to dispute the decision.

Context: We have multiple types of blocking, but the process for contestation varies.

Drivers can officially contest the following blockings:

* Driver Score-related blockings
* Verification-related blockings



In both cases, drivers receive communications that their request has been escalated to another team to evaluate the contestation eligibility or are encouraged to contest the blocking decision if they disagree with it.

However, we don’t have an appeal process for events where drivers are blocked for:

* Behavior-related events
* Acceptance rate
* Statistical blocking (High cancellation rate, low average rating score)
* Fraudulent orders



The blocking above can be temporary or infinite.



Questions:

* Do you believe CS needs any official communications once sharing with the driver that their account has been permanently blocked?
* Is it aligned with your team's expectations that drivers can only contest certain types of blocking?

Many thanks!

Hi all,

I think the problem with this EC is that we have not defined what a robbery is and with which reports it goes.  The current  EC description is an event in which the rider robbed or attempted to rob the driver which leaves it open to interpretation. I sense a certain fear among agents to miss safety incidents and therefore they are more likely to interpret all the reports as robbery just to be on the safe side.

Because of this, we are seeing a lot of cases where:
 1. drivers don’t have a change in case of a cash trip (rider reports they were *robbed* in clear daylight as the saying goes)
2. riders are taking the driver’s (low-value) personal items when leaving the car either by accident or on purpose. We’ve had reports of lost jackets, water bottles, grocery bags, a Halloween mask etc
3. riders leaving the car without paying in case of a cash trip (driver claims he was r*obbed* of his time and gas)

The list can go on. If necessary, we can find ticket examples. 

So, essentially, the agents are putting robbery and stealing into one pot. As a solution, I’d propose one of these two options:

1. Changing the EC description to explain it better. According to the definition, robbery is taking property [unlawfull|https://www.google.com/search?sca_esv=ebc234f9216407d8&sca_upv=1&rlz=1C5CHFA_enEE989EE989&q=unlawfully&si=AKbGX_pt4UlL1m2gNC94R_NJDj6SoBiYBcJs0M4xwYBqxZDKOLjoiLIR3lZy_MA6w3Ygf2BGGpXG2eqgt3MHjlqRxKa_8BPspPV8XUzVgFAUgmG5LtlT2BM%3D&expnd=1]y from (a person or place) by *force or threat of force.* Therefore,  the new description could be “An event in which the rider robbed or attempted to rob the driver using force or threats of force”. 

2. Creating a new  Low/Moderate EC Driver Stole or Attempted to Steal from Rider.  This way we could differentiate between robberies and stealing. 

I would prefer updating the Robbery EC description as robberies are related to user’s safety. Stealing something is more of a behavioural issue and as it does not include threats or force it can even be argued if it’s a safety issue anymore.

What do you think?

Kadri

* [~accountid:621d26539c3cce00694a1b14] and I finalised the memo with all the details regarding this project and highlighting the legal angles, risks as well as proposing some mitigations measures: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HWCfYa7p4aBKB7ClftkkHkxuUC8He9eokwzE0cNo-9k/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HWCfYa7p4aBKB7ClftkkHkxuUC8He9eokwzE0cNo-9k/edit|smart-link]
* Emilie instructed Osborne Clarke to get clarifications on our questions.

5 Avril:

We received the feedback from Osborne Clarke. Pls find below a summary and here [their full advice|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ze8ibo-zxFL4kHi8r6suyi036_hQHkvvoKFXJwfJE5g/edit].

+*Reclassification risks*+: {color:#ff5630}MEDIUM TO HIGH{color}

* As anticipated, they agree that offering this EV Project to *Fleet Owners only* (_and not to independent / private drivers_) *will significantly lower the risk of reclassification*.
* However, *even if this offer is limited to Fleet Owners* (FOs), *the reclassification risks would remain medium to high*.
* Their +recommendations+ are therefore as follows:
** *Only include FOs*, ie a B2B partnership (not private drivers;
** *Send the offer to all FOs and not by priority to the trusted FOs* (who already perform their services mainly for Bolt). 
** *Reduce the duration of the contract to* *12 months renewable*
** *Provide the possibility to freely negotiate certain clauses* (e.g. monthly KPI's, exclusivity, etc.). 
** *Mitigate the reasons to terminate the contract for gross misconduct* (could be perceived as a sanction) - _Nb: I am clarifying this with OC and asking them for examples/wording_

+*Risk of unauthorized advertising*+: {color:#bf2600}MEDIUM TO HIGH{color}

* As for the other branded cars in BE, for this project the sticker with the *legal disclaimer "**_non-exclusive affiliation with the Bolt booking intermediary_**" needs to be affixed* on all cars.
* *However this does not completely protect Bolt* from the risks of unauthorized advertising. 
* *The green colour all over the cars could be seen as unnecessary to simply inform about the affiliation to Bolt and therefore increases the risk that it will be considered as advertising even with the disclaimer*.
* +Potential consequences+:
** Brussels Mobility could prohibit Bolt from using advertising signs and green colour.;
** Being in breach of the Brussels Taxi Regulation can constitute an *offense punishable by a prison sentence* (between 8 days and 3 months) and/or a *fine of up to €80K*;
** Competitors could launch a cease-and-desist action in order to obtain an injunction to cease the use of all the advertising signs.

+*Risk of Greenwashing & misleading commercial practice*+*:* {color:#ff991f}MEDIUM{color}

* The colour green is linked to ecology and is used by some industries to participate in greenwashing strategies.
* It is therefore *not recommended to invoke the fact that the colour green is linked to ecology as it could potentially lead to accusations of greenwashing and be considered as misleading commercial practice*. 
* +Potential consequences+:
** The regulator could request us to modify or remove the advertisement deemed misleading or false.  
** This could also lead to a *legal cease-and-desist action* brought by the Minister of Economy or a competitor.
** The Minister of Economy has also the authority to investigate and impose a Level 2 fine which consists of a *criminal fine* (max €80K or 4% of the total annual sales turnover).

+*Contract*+:

* *The existence of a contract between Bolt and the FO may increase the risk of unauthorized advertising*. 
* We could envisage a branding contract, ideally based upon the current branding terms, however this approach carries a risk due to the subtle distinction between branding and advertising, which can be tight in practice.

{color:#0747a6}+*Conclusion*+{color}{color:#0747a6}:{color}

{color:#0747a6}The risks are relatively high however, unless Product Legal ({color}{color:#0747a6}_cc_ {color}[~accountid:619e455ab43d5b006a05c173]{color:#0747a6} {color}[~accountid:612f31d89976c300693ebaf7]{color:#0747a6} {color}[~accountid:62722e092db308007024a425]{color:#0747a6}) informs us of any specific guidelines / process for such decision, my understanding is that the decision of launching this EV project lies with the Country Manager, based on an informed decision of the risks, to be balanced with the anticipated ROI.{color}

Hi, all! Answering your questions:

* *What is the ultimate goal that we want to reach with this tool?*

The ultimate goal is to ensure that Bolt value proposition to riders and drivers remain optimal in the market place. Getting this intel will give use more understanding of our friends Net rate and value prop to drivers.

* *What personal data will be available there? Could you give me a list of all the data that would be put there?*

Rolle won’t be sharing personal data by driver, but an aggregation of the drivers that use their app (Bolt and Uber drivers):

# Number of drivers (using the Rollee app)
# Number of trips taken
# Total driver net income
# Supply spend
# Online hours


* *How would the onboarding look like? Will Rollee have an integration with Bolt, or will it be separate?*

Bolt wouldn’t be onboarding any drivers, Rollee would act as a data provider. And will share the data they have from the drivers that are using the app. 

* *Will we have any access to data collected from platforms other than Bolt?*

Yes, Rollee would provide us data on all the data shared to them from both Bolt and Uber drivers.

I submitted the ticket to IT to disable Playmode. 

However, I wanted to mention that we don't recommend removing playmode for new hires. 

Here are some benefits to be aware of: 

*Cherry picking versus Skipping* - Cherry picking of cases won't leave any trace of potential knowledge gaps or any data for trainers to follow up on. Skipping of cases will allow trainers to have visibility on which topics the agent needs retraining. 

*New hires showing higher productivity thanks to cherry-picking versus new hires showing performance metrics according to the real knowledge consolidation* - agents that are allowed to cherry-pick will have limited knowledge on subjects they will not pick, with Play Mode view agents will need to handle a variety of subjects, also there is the possibility of picking up certain subjects that trainer believes that should be handled on the given day is possible by him as agents on Play Mode can be still be provided with case links and assign those to themselves.

Feel free to submit a new ticket when you want to have the agent back on Playmode. 

I will inform you when the playmode is removed.

* And manyy redundant steps removed.

Some updates from the Fiscal Authority (ANAF), regarding the data sharing with the authority. I will copy paste here what ANAF proposed:

(1) 

* a monthly statement for platforms, providing in a standardised form the type of information/data on transport operators (same data they asked us before but in a more standardised form). 
* the platform will have to file that statement every month for the previous month. It's an informative statement that is aimed at increasing tax conformity among transport operators (knowing we file this every month, transport operators will be less inclined to avoid paying taxes). 
* this introduction of statement should set (more or less) a T0 in the cooperation, with the tax inspectors unlikely to focus on historical data, save for any major exceptions.

(2)

* ANAF to send seizure to the representative office of the platform (sent to local entity, which according to the RH law and intra group agreement, it represents the interests of the Estonian entity in relation to RO authorities) asking the platform to block any future payments to an operator that failed to pay its debts to the state. 
* *An operator that hasn't pay 100k in taxes, the platform needs to hold future payments of 100k and transfer these due payments for the operator in a Treasury account until the issue is cleared by the operator and tax office*.

*ANAF wants to prepare better the two things above and they will invite operators to discuss them in detail in a week or so.*

Hi [Ekaterina] - thanks for your patience on this one 🙂 

In short there’s a couple of tax / billing / other things to sync on internally before the launches proceed, but generally our launches are not conditional on updating T+Cs in most markets (there is an exception on this for *Netherlands*, *France*, *Belgium* and *Germany*), nor on conducting additional legal research.

+*(1) The need for additional legal research / investigations*+

Considering Bolt’s key principles of being ‘quick’, ‘frugal’ and ‘pragmatic’ etc., we generally consider that the risk profile associated with Early Cashouts does not warrant additional ‘per market legal’ research.

_(Note: we previously sought legal advice in relation to the launch of this feature in the UK, a highly regulated market, and we were ultimately comfortably with launching on the basis of the advice received.)_

+*(2) The need to update terms and conditions: different rules for different markets*+

Our terms *_should_* be updated to support this feature. However, considering the risk profile, Bolt’s key principles (as mentioned above) and the desire to launch the feature ASAP, we can facilitate our terms being updated at a later date (throughout 2024). This approach deliberately prioritises the commercial needs over the need to mitigate the known risk profile.

However *Netherlands*, *France*, *Belgium* and *Germany* are exceptions to this: the terms for those markets must be updated first. This is because those markets are known to be more sensitive. The timing of the launch in those markets will therefore need to be pragmatic based on the status of those markets (e.g. whether any other features are being launched, whether any other changes to terms are due and whether it would make more sense for timings to sync etc.). I will sync. with the local counsel for those markets but in the meantime, are the timings on the confluence page still the proposed timings?

+*(3) True Fleets / Fleet Markets*+

I anticipate this will already have been foreseen / accommodated, but the feature cannot obviously be introduced to any driver that is a ‘true fleet driver’ (e.g. where the fleet driver gets paid by the fleet). We have no control over when ‘true fleet drivers’ will get paid by their fleet. In fact, Bolt does not even have a contractual relationship with ‘true fleet drivers’ as they act as sub-contractees of fleets. This means the advertising and visibility of the feature should be targeted accordingly (i.e. not at fleet drivers).

For certainty, has this been considered / taken into account? If not, this will need to be considered prior to launch.

+*(4) Early Cashouts Can Only Apply to Cleared Funds*+

This point universally applies with the exception of any ‘principal market’ - such the the UK private hire market. However, any ‘true taxi’ market in the UK (such as London black cabs) will not fall within this exception.

In all ‘standard agency model markets’ we should only pass over cash via Early Cashouts if it has cleared in our accounts. Otherwise Bolt will be paying the money out of its own pocket, which is inappropriate for several reasons.

^This is essential to review ahead of the launch.

+*(5) Keeping fees low - a good way of mitigating risk*+

The higher our fees, the more likely they will annoy people and/or prompt regulator review. In theory, we can reduce the risk of this by ensuring that our fees are proportionate and reasonable (e.g. not ridiculous). We want to be seen as providing a legitimate option and flexibility for drivers, not using it as another excuse to make a quick buck. There is no absolute rule to follow here, but I understand that our fees are generally less than 1% of the average cashout which suggests to me that we are the right side of the line. 

+*(6) Tax and billing*+

From the tax side, our internal tax team needs to confirm the applicable rate of VAT that applies to our charges (if any). This might different from the rates that apply to our commission. From the billing side, we need to be clear that we are ready to accomodate these fees on our invoices - following the tax position.

^This is essential to review ahead of the launch - [fedde] [franco] do you have any comments on this?

Separately, although it is not essential for launch, we really ought to issue interim invoices at the point of the Early Cashout as this helps makes it clear that we are treating the drivers as an independent business. 

+*(7) Communications*+

In addition to the point on fleets above, all of our standard guidance on comms. will continue to apply - see [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONTENT/pages/4468998200/Reclassification+Risk+Copy+Guide]. In particular, we must avoid suggesting that we are giving anyone an ‘advancement of wages’ because Bolt does not pay drivers wages: drivers do {color:#ff5630}+*NOT*+{color} work for Bolt. Likewise, we are absolutely {color:#ff5630}+*NOT*+{color} providing any sort of credit or loan (as this would be a regulated activity).

Hi [~accountid:5d50390ec6b9320d9ea58352] - thanks for your patience on this one 🙏 

There’s some things to sync on internally before the launches proceed (re: tax, cleared funds, billing and fleets if we haven’t sorted those points already) but generally our launches globally will not be conditional on updating T+Cs in advance. There are a few exceptions to (i.e *Netherlands*, *France*, *Belgium* and *Germany*) because of recent regulator activity - more info below!

----

{color:#0747a6}+*(1) The need for additional legal research / investigations*+{color}

Considering Bolt’s key principles of being ‘quick’, ‘frugal’ and ‘pragmatic’ etc., we generally consider that the risk profile associated with Early Cashouts does not warrant additional ‘per market legal’ research. 

h6. _(Note: we previously sought legal advice in relation to the launch of this feature in the UK, a highly regulated market, and we were ultimately comfortably with launching on the basis of the advice received.)_

{color:#0747a6}+*(2) The need to update terms and conditions: different rules for different markets*+{color}

Our terms should be updated to support this feature. However, considering the risk profile, Bolt’s key principles and the desire to launch the feature ASAP, we can instead facilitate our terms being updated at a later date (throughout 2024). This approach deliberately prioritises the commercial needs over the need to mitigate the known risk profile.

However *Netherlands*, *France*, *Belgium* and *Germany* are exceptions to this: {color:#ff5630}the terms for those markets must be updated first{color}. This is because those markets are known to be more sensitive due to recent regulator activity. The timing of the launch in these markets will therefore need to be pragmatic based on the status of those markets (e.g. whether any other features are being launched, whether any other changes to terms are due and whether it would make more sense for timings to sync etc.). 

I will mention this launch to the local counsel in those markets but in the meantime, are the timings on the confluence page still the proposed timings?

{color:#0747a6}+*(3) ‘True Fleets’ / Fleet Markets*+{color}

I anticipate this will already have been foreseen / accommodated, but the feature cannot obviously be introduced to any driver that is a ‘true fleet driver’ (e.g. where the fleet driver gets paid by the fleet). We have no control over when ‘true fleet drivers’ will get paid by their fleet. In fact, Bolt does not even have a contractual relationship with ‘true fleet drivers’ as they act as sub-contractees of fleets. This means the advertising and visibility of the feature should be targeted accordingly (i.e. not at fleet drivers).

For certainty, has this been considered / taken into account? If not, this will need to be considered prior to launch so that we are not sending fleet drivers inappropriate messages. 

{color:#0747a6}+*(4) Early Cashouts can only apply to cleared funds*+{color}

This point universally applies with the exception of any ‘principal market’ - such the the UK private hire market. However, any ‘true taxi’ market in the UK (such as London black cabs) will not fall within this exception.

In all ‘standard agency model markets’ we should only pass over cash via Early Cashouts if it has cleared in our accounts. Otherwise Bolt will be paying the money out of its own pocket, which is inappropriate for several reasons.

{color:#ff5630}^This is essential to review ahead of the launch{color}

{color:#0747a6}+*(5) Keeping fees low - a good way of mitigating risk*+{color}

The higher our fees, the more likely they will annoy people and/or prompt regulator review. In theory, we can reduce the risk of this by ensuring that our fees are proportionate and reasonable (e.g. not ridiculous). We want to be seen as providing a legitimate option and flexibility for drivers, not using it as another excuse to make a quick buck. There is no absolute rule to follow here, but I understand that our fees are generally less than 1% of the average cashout which suggests to me that we are the right side of the line.

{color:#0747a6}+*(6) Tax and billing*+{color}

From the tax side, our internal tax team needs to confirm the applicable rate of VAT that applies to our charges (if any). This might different from the rates that apply to our commission. From the billing side, we need to be clear that we are ready to accomodate these fees on our invoices - following the tax position.

{color:#ff5630}^This is essential to review ahead of the launch {color}- [~accountid:607d9ec5a41c7a007832afa1] [~accountid:62615f256cb53d006a6a3fe1] [~accountid:616fd13725f3130070530ffd] do you have any comments on this?

Separately, although it is not essential for launch, we really ought to issue interim invoices at the point of the Early Cashout as this helps makes it clear that we are treating the drivers as an independent business. [~accountid:616fd13725f3130070530ffd] do you have any recommendations as to who I can raise this with? 🙂 

{color:#0747a6}+*(7) Communications*+{color}

In addition to the point on fleets above, all of our standard guidance on comms. will continue to apply - see [{color:#ff5630}+here+{color}|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONTENT/pages/4468998200/Reclassification+Risk+Copy+Guide]. In particular, we must avoid suggesting that we are giving anyone an ‘advancement of wages’ because Bolt does not pay drivers wages: drivers do {color:#ff5630}+*NOT*+{color} work for Bolt. Likewise, we are absolutely {color:#ff5630}+*NOT*+{color} providing any sort of credit or loan (as this would be a regulated activity).

----

Let me know if you have any questions - thanks 👌

h3. How it works now (all calculations are for one company)

h4. Due balance data (unpaid amount which hasn't passed the due date yet)

* Calculate {{invoiced_outflow}}:
** sum up all aggregated records;
* Calculated {{inflow}}:
** sum up all “positive balance changes without refunds” – bank transfers, topups, rebates, apology credits, etc.;
** sum up all “not-yet-invoiced refunds”;
* Calculate final {{invoiced_balance}} ={{inflow}} - {{invoiced_outflow}}.

*SQL Example*

{code:sql}-- invoiced balance
-- select the latest aggregated record
SELECT id, period_end_ts
FROM aggregated_record ar
WHERE ar.business_company_id = 74607
  AND ar.is_deleted = 0
ORDER BY id DESC
LIMIT 1;

-- calculate the inflow and invoiced outflow
SELECT bc.id                             AS business_company_id,
       IFNULL(
               (SELECT SUM(be_united.sum)
                FROM (SELECT be.sum
                      FROM `balance_entry` be
                           LEFT JOIN `adjustment` adj
                                     ON be.type = 'adjustment' AND be.reference_id = adj.id
                           LEFT JOIN `rebate` r
                                     ON be.type = 'rebate' AND be.reference_id = r.id
                      WHERE be.type IN
                            ('bank_transfer', 'topup', 'rebate', 'apology_credit', 'adjustment', 'withholding_tax')
                        AND (adj.id IS NULL OR adj.is_hidden = 0)
                        AND (r.id IS NULL OR r.self_invoice_creation_state = 'finished')
                        AND be.business_company_id = 74607

                      UNION ALL

                      SELECT rr.sum_with_vat
                      FROM `record` rr
                           JOIN `record` ro ON rr.claim_id = ro.claim_id
                      WHERE rr.type = 'refund'
                        AND (ro.type = 'business_order' OR ro.type = 'service_fee')
                        AND rr.to_agent_id = 74607
                        AND rr.to_agent_type = 'business_company'
                        AND rr.action_timestamp > '2024-03-31 22:59:59'
                        AND ro.action_timestamp <= '2024-03-31 22:59:59') be_united),
               0
       )                                 AS inflow,
       (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(a_subquery.total_sum_with_vat), 0)
        FROM `aggregated_record` a_subquery
        WHERE a_subquery.business_company_id = bc.id
          AND a_subquery.is_deleted = 0) AS invoiced_outflow
FROM `business_company` bc
WHERE bc.id = 74607;{code}

h4. Overdue balance data (unpaid amount which has passed the due date)

* Calculate {{invoiced_outflow}}:
** sum up all overdue aggregated records ({{payment_due_ts < NOW()}});
* Calculated {{inflow}}:
** sum up all “positive balance changes without refunds” – bank transfers, topups, rebates, apology credits, etc.;
** sum up all “not-yet-invoiced refunds”;
* Calculate final {{overdue_invoiced_balance}} ={{inflow}} - {{invoiced_outflow}}.

*SQL Example*

{noformat}-- overdue balance
-- select the latest overdue record
SELECT id, period_end_ts
FROM aggregated_record ar
WHERE ar.business_company_id = 74607
  AND ar.is_deleted = 0
  AND ar.payment_due_ts < NOW()
ORDER BY id DESC
LIMIT 1;

-- calculate the inflow and invoiced outflow
SELECT bc.id AS business_company_id,
       IFNULL(
               (SELECT SUM(be_united.sum)
                FROM (SELECT be.sum
                      FROM `balance_entry` be
                           LEFT JOIN `adjustment` adj
                                     ON be.type = 'adjustment' AND be.reference_id = adj.id
                           LEFT JOIN `rebate` r
                                     ON be.type = 'rebate' AND be.reference_id = r.id
                      WHERE be.type IN
                            ('bank_transfer', 'topup', 'rebate', 'apology_credit', 'adjustment', 'withholding_tax')
                        AND (adj.id IS NULL OR adj.is_hidden = 0)
                        AND (r.id IS NULL OR r.self_invoice_creation_state = 'finished')
                        AND be.business_company_id = 74607

                      UNION ALL

                      SELECT rr.sum_with_vat
                      FROM `record` rr
                           JOIN `record` ro ON rr.claim_id = ro.claim_id
                      WHERE rr.type = 'refund'
                        AND (ro.type = 'business_order' OR ro.type = 'service_fee')
                        AND rr.to_agent_id = 74607
                        AND rr.to_agent_type = 'business_company'
                        AND rr.action_timestamp > '2024-02-29 23:59:59'
                        AND ro.action_timestamp <= '2024-02-29 23:59:59') be_united),
               0
       )     AS inflow,

       (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(a_subquery.total_sum_with_vat), 0)
        FROM `aggregated_record` a_subquery
        WHERE a_subquery.business_company_id = bc.id
          AND a_subquery.is_deleted = 0
          AND a_subquery.payment_due_ts < NOW())
             AS invoiced_outflow
FROM `business_company` bc
WHERE bc.id = 74607;{noformat}

h3. How it can work

[https://excalidraw.com/#room=de95af56c36a0bc56405,GStJRclwpWtRPou9RDtzVA|https://excalidraw.com/#room=de95af56c36a0bc56405,GStJRclwpWtRPou9RDtzVA|smart-link]

h4. Due balance data

* Take business company {{balance}};
* Calculate {{not_invoiced_sum}}:
** sum up all non-invoiced records ({{r.aggregated_record_id IS NULL}});
* Calculate {{refunds_sum_for_invoiced_records}}:
** sum up all non-invoiced refunds with invoiced reference record ({{r.aggregated_record_id IS NULL AND rr.aggregated_record_id IS NOT NULL}});
* Calculate final {{invoiced_balance}} = {{balance}} + {{not_invoiced_sum}} - {{refunds_sum_for_invoiced_records}}.

*SQL Example*

{code:sql}-- new invoiced balance
-- get business company balance
SELECT bc.id AS business_company_id,
       bc.balance
FROM business_company bc
WHERE bc.id = 305488;

-- calculate non_invoiced sum
SELECT IFNULL(SUM(IF(r.to_agent_type = 'business_company', -r.sum_with_vat, r.sum_with_vat)), 0) AS sum
FROM record r
WHERE ((r.from_agent_id = 305488
    AND r.from_agent_type = 'business_company')
    OR (r.to_agent_id = 305488 AND r.to_agent_type = 'business_company'))
  AND r.aggregated_record_id IS NULL;

-- calculate refunds sum for invoiced records
SELECT IFNULL(SUM(-r.sum_with_vat), 0) AS sum
FROM record r
     LEFT JOIN record rr ON r.ref_record_id = rr.id
WHERE r.to_agent_id = 305488
  AND r.to_agent_type = 'business_company'
  AND r.aggregated_record_id IS NULL
  AND rr.aggregated_record_id IS NOT NULL;{code}

h4. Overdue balance data

* Take business company {{balance}};
* Calculate {{non_overdue_aggregate_records_sum}};
* Calculate {{not_invoiced_sum}}:
** sum up all non-invoiced records ({{r.aggregated_record_id IS NULL}});
* Calculate {{refunds for overdue sum}};
* Calculate final {{invoiced_balance}} = {{balance}} + {{not_invoiced_sum}} + {{non_overdue_aggregate_records_sum}} - {{refunds_for_overdue_sum}}.

*SQL Example*

{code:sql}-- new overdue balance
-- get business company balance
SELECT bc.id AS business_company_id,
       bc.balance
FROM business_company bc
WHERE bc.id = 305488;

-- get non_overdue_aggregate_records_sum
SELECT SUM(total_sum_with_vat)
FROM aggregated_record
WHERE business_company_id = 305488
  AND is_deleted = 0
  AND payment_due_ts > NOW();

-- calculate non_invoiced sum
SELECT IFNULL(SUM(IF(r.to_agent_type = 'business_company', -r.sum_with_vat, r.sum_with_vat)), 0) AS sum
FROM record r
WHERE ((r.from_agent_id = 305488
    AND r.from_agent_type = 'business_company')
    OR (r.to_agent_id = 305488 AND r.to_agent_type = 'business_company'))
  AND r.aggregated_record_id IS NULL;

-- calculate refunds for overdue sum
SELECT IFNULL(SUM(-r.sum_with_vat), 0) AS sum
FROM record r
     LEFT JOIN record rr ON r.ref_record_id = rr.id
WHERE r.to_agent_id = 305488
  AND r.to_agent_type = 'business_company'
  AND rr.aggregated_record_id IN (7704276); -- id overdue aggregated records{code}

Cause of this behavior is that the presigned URL cannot be valid beyond the expiration of the temporary credentials used when generating it. In our case, the temporary credentials are those generated by the AWS SDK when it starts up (and are refreshed automatically approx 2 min before they expire - assuming they are actually used, or on first use after expiry).

The only solution that comes to my mind to reliably fix this is to use an S3 client with persistent credentials (belonging to an IAM User) to generate presigned URLs.

The best approach would be to allow service code to pass in an S3 client or credential configuration to the {{S3StorageBackend}} upon initialization. The service would be responsible to read the IAM User credentials from Secrets storage.

Ideas to reduce the impact on the security posture (because we start using long-lived secrets):

* The IAM user’s permissions should be scoped down as much as possible. I see we currently generate presigned URLs only for download, but if we start generating them for upload, I think it makes sense to require a different IAM user
* Extract the presigned URL logic into a new specialized component outside of {{S3StorageBackend}}. This allows using the other methods with temporary credentials, and use persistent credentials only for presigned URLs
* Have some sort of procedure / automation to periodically rotate IAM user credentials.

SK has level/class 2. Regarding premium quality policy removal then we see that it is ok to remove it from couriers whose performance is low. If risk level should be 1 or 3, then our advice at leas currently would be the same.
