In case it is agreed in the fleet agreement that fleet cannot disclose this info to its couriers etc, then risks ar lower. If you want to discuss this topic more with me, then let me know.

* In general, we have drawn the process for handling law enforcement requests for a dual reason - to assist the police as fast as possible and to stay in line with the requirements of privacy laws, such as the GDPR.
✅ 

* In short, when we receive a request from the police to disclose personal data to them, we need to assess the validity and proportionality of this request. While we do not dig too deep into the crime itself, we need to assess whether the police is acting in a proportional manner, for example, that they don’t ask 5 years worth of order history to investigate a littering case.
_This is not aligned with what Dutch police claims. As they are not legally allowed to share any ongoing investigations with us, they cannot possibly share this data. They also mention_ *_it is not up to us to decide what is proportional and what is not._* 
--> *_The Criminal Procedure Act supersedes the EU GDPR law in the Netherlands._*

* in order to stay in line with the requirements of Articles 5 and 6 of the GDPR, we need to have a legal basis to share the data.
_If we receive a demand from the police (officially known as a "police requisition"), we are legally obliged to provide the requested data to the police. The content of the requisition is irrelevant in this regard, according to Dutch police._

Please let me know if you agree with this, so we can incorporate this into our process for CS when they receive official police requests.

Best,

Hey Thomas ,

In order to create base fee calculators, we would need the following information:

* *Commission rate*: Commission percentage that will apply per ride to the driver/fleet.
* *Currency*: Usually country default if not stated otherwise
* *Invoicing strategy*: Driver or Company. This will define to whom payouts will go, and invoices will be issued.
* *Booking fee:* Is there an active booking fee in the city? If so, do you want it to be deducted from the driver (and reflected on the commission invoice), or be a 100% driver income?
* *Cash-blocking thresholds*: Defines the cash ride limits for blocking/unblocking cash rides for a driver. This can be copied from other cities, but please discuss with [{color:#b3f5ff}Billing Analytics{color}|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/1240/create/806] if your market is cash-heavy.
** Max negative balance before messaging: The threshold where we will notify the driver that they are getting closer to being cash-blocked
** Max negative balance before removing cash payments: The debt threshold we allow cash rides up to. After the driver exceeds this threshold, cash orders will be disabled.
** Minimal balance to unblock cash rides: The balance threshold where we will once again unblock the driver’s cash rides.
* *List of company_ids you want this fee calculator to be attached to*.

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*What is a Base Fee Calculator*

It is a default fee calculator template created by Billing team in order for local operations teams to easily attach the relevant fee calculator to new companies. [Please read this guide to see how|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/1603928517/Base+fee+calculators].
{panel}

* Re point 2, as we discussed yesterday, it is a Commerce (FinReg and Commerce Legal) requirement that T&Cs must properly describe early payout feature. Ideally, T&Cs change should take place prior to feature launch. If there is a justified need to delay T&Cs change, we need to agree clear roll-out roadmap (without any unjustified delay). We should have an agreed wording in place for this
* Re point 4, it is not fully true that we only do early payout in case we have received money from passenger; we may also do it before this, in case there is a payment failure or in case of monthly billing of Bolt Business customer. However, this is a regulatory risk we are exposed to already today, because same this applies also to weekly payouts (only exception being that enabling early payouts may slightly increase the amount that are paid out prior to successful collection). Thus, in regulated credit context we focus on making payouts for services already performed by the service provider (and not that much on the successful payment from the users).

# We rediscussed the topic with our legal/GDPR team

Until the Personal Data is deleted or returned, the Processor shall continue to ensure compliance with this Annex.”_

 

 

Their comment on your question below is the following:

_“It seems to me that the client controller did not understand exactly: these are original documents only for which an implicit data processing is done. These documents (except for those that must remain with Mazars) Mazars_ +_undertakes to return them to the client controller_+_, not to destroy them (for example following the instruction of data deletion of the client controller), given that the Romanian law on destruction of documents is very restrictive and regulates prior formalities and prior authorization for such an action._

_In other words, please, the aspect outlined in that clause in my view is that, on the contrary, the original documents will be returned, they are not implicitly destroyed following the instruction of the client controller to delete / to destroy no needed any more for processing personal data._

_If you/the client controller have/has a wording of the respective clause that it considers clearer in the light of the above, it can be of course suggested/ communicated. But, allow me to repeat, it is not about retaining the originals that must be returned to the client controller.”_

As mentioned before, we re-assessed internally Bolt’s standard position to extend the liability for confidentiality and data protections breaches *to indirect damages*, and *we have decided to accept* your proposal.

Hi,

Why it is happened?

h1. Hidden Rider Invoices

In some cases we generate the invoices as “hidden” invoices - they do exist in the system with the subtype “statement” and they are hidden (they are not sent to the riders, they cannot be downloaded from the Rider App and they cannot be downloaded from the Admin Panel either). The reason why we even create these entries - Finance and Accounting.

First case - the “Send invoice info for cash payment method” option is unchecked on the company’s profile. In this case the invoices are hidden for payment methods where the rider pays directly to the driver on the spot after the ride (cash or card terminal). So driver had to provide an invoice in this case!

Second case - the issuer and the recipient are the same. It’s not legal to issue an invoice to oneself so in case the driver's registry code and the rider’s registry code are identical, the invoice will be hidden.

Hi,

Sometimes invoice generation is skipped for certain reasons. In such cases, you’d see the following errors under Invoice Tasks tab in the driver/fleet profile (in Admin v2):

* {{EXAMPLE: Invoice sum too small: -11.2, period 2022-04-01 - 2022-07-31}}: The invoice sum for the period is negative (i.e. when their bonuses/compensations are more than the commission we charge). In that case, we don’t generate invoice for that period, but transfer that period to the next invoicing period (next month for drivers/fleets). This keeps happening until the commission becomes more than the sum of their bonuses. Then we generate the invoice starting from the first skipped invoice period.

If to check the client page: [https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-rides/clients/218185197?tab=invoice_tasks&filter={"limit"%3A25%2C"offset"%3A0%2C"filter"%3A{}}&tz=Europe%2FTallinn|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-rides/clients/218185197?tab=invoice_tasks&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn]

Hi,

Why this happened:

h1. Hidden Rider Invoices

In some cases we generate the invoices as “hidden” invoices - they do exist in the system with the subtype “statement” and they are hidden (they are not sent to the riders, they cannot be downloaded from the Rider App and they cannot be downloaded from the Admin Panel either). The reason why we even create these entries - Finance and Accounting.

First case - the “Send invoice info for cash payment method” option is unchecked on the company’s profile. In this case the invoices are hidden for payment methods where the rider pays directly to the driver on the spot after the ride (cash or card terminal).  _> Driver had to provide it at the car

Second case - the issuer and the recipient are the same. It’s not legal to issue an invoice to oneself so in case the driver's registry code and the rider’s registry code are identical, the invoice will be hidden.

Hi [~accountid:712020:548c71a6-d1f4-404d-9c5e-482bc0de371a] 

please find below some legal requirements for FR, BE and IT.

*FR and BE:* please make sure Terms and Conditions of the Prize Draw are made available and accepted by participants. T&Cs must include eligibility conditions, prize description, prize draw date and instructions to claim the prize. Personal data are usually processed so this should be covered in the T&Cs or by separate privacy notice.

*IT:* requirements are very tricky and include : 

* *Terms and conditions* including the following: 
** *Deliver the prizes:* according to Italian law, prizes must be awarded within 180 days, and the delivery should be certified and verifiable. If we can’t deliver the prize, or there is no winner, then we should donate the prize to a non-profit organization. 
** *Non-profit organizations:* we must nominate a non-profit organization in our terms and conditions, in case there are problems delivering the prize.
* *Guarantee the prize value:* we need to appoin a a guarantor or make a deposit in the Bank of Italy, to show that we are offering a genuine prize.
* *Official form:* we need to fill in an official form with information about the prize draw *at least 15 days before* the promotion starts and submit it online to the Ministry for Economic Development ([+Ministero del Sviluppo Economico+|https://www.mise.gov.it/index.php/it/]). The document should be sent by *an IT resident* with an authorized digital signature. 
* We must either have an IT permanent establishment or have a tax representative in Italy. 
* we must use contests software which is secure and fair. The server processing contest data should be located in Italian territory or ensuring *a mirroring service in Italy.* _I believe that we are relying on AWS data hosting systems which AFAIK are not located in IT and mirroring services are expensive._ 
* *Awarding prizes:* The winner selection should take place in front of a public notary, in the province where the prize is awarded. _Notaries in IT are bloody expensive._
* *Taxes:* Bolt must pay tax on prizes in contests. That includes a withholding tax of 25% of the prize’s sale price of the prize. You can’t recover VAT on goods or services which you purchase for prizes, so they have a further effective tax rate of 22%. If the goods or services are VAT-free, then you have to apply a substitute tax of 20% of the purchase value.

Considering the above complexity, you might want to carve out IT from the launch batch. 

Please let me know if you need additional clarification.

Best regards, 

Michela

COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_initial_failed_payment THEN x.initial_failed_eur END) AS double),2),0) AS initial_fp_sum_eur,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_initial_failed_payment THEN x.initial_failed_eur END) AS double),2),0)*1.000/SUM(x.user_price_eur) AS double),3),0) AS initial_fp_sum_ratio,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.is_final_failed_payment THEN x.order_id END,0.0041) AS count_fp,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.is_final_failed_payment THEN x.order_id END,0.0041)*1.000/APPROX_DISTINCT(x.order_id,0.0041) AS double),3),0) AS ratio_fp,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_final_failed_payment THEN x.failed_payment_eur END) AS double),2),0) AS fp_sum_eur,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_final_failed_payment THEN x.failed_payment_eur END) AS double),2),0)*1.000/SUM(x.user_price_eur) AS double),3),0) AS fp_sum_ratio,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.is_chargeback THEN x.order_id END,0.0041) AS count_cb,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.is_chargeback THEN x.order_id END,0.0041)*1.00/APPROX_DISTINCT(x.order_id,0.0041) AS double),2),0) AS ratio_cb,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_chargeback THEN x.fraud_loss_eur END) AS double),2),0) AS cb_sum_eur,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_chargeback THEN x.fraud_loss_eur END) AS double),2),0)*1.00/SUM(x.user_price_eur) AS double),2),0) AS cb_sum_ratio,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem THEN x.order_id END,0.0041) AS count_pp,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem THEN x.order_id END,0.0041)*1.00/APPROX_DISTINCT(x.order_id,0.0041) AS double),2),0) AS ratio_pp,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem THEN x.fraud_loss_eur END) AS double),2),0) AS pp_sum_eur,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem THEN x.fraud_loss_eur END) AS double),2),0)*1.00/SUM(x.user_price_eur) AS double),2),0) AS pp_sum_ratio
FROM (
WITH has_waypoint_change AS (
SELECT 
a.order_id,
a.city_id
FROM ng_public.pricing_order_prediction a
WHERE a.created_date >= date '2023-01-01'
AND a.change_reason = 'driver_waypoint_changed'
)
SELECT DISTINCT 
co.created,
date(date_trunc('day',co.created)) AS day,
date(date_trunc('week',co.created)) AS week,
date(date_trunc('month',co.created)) AS month,
co.order_id,
co.city_id,
co.country_code,
co.is_payment_problem,
co.is_chargeback,
co.is_initial_failed_payment,
co.is_final_failed_payment,
co.initial_failed_payment_amount/co.eur_currency_rate AS initial_failed_eur,
co.uncovered_amount/co.eur_currency_rate AS failed_payment_eur,
co.fraud_loss/co.eur_currency_rate AS fraud_loss_eur,
co.user_price_eur
FROM has_waypoint_change a
JOIN ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co ON a.order_id = co.order_id AND a.city_id = co.city_id
WHERE co.created_date >= date '2023-01-01'
AND co.order_type = 'rides'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
) AS x 
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, 2{code}

(2) Any natural person who has reasonable cause to believe to be a beneficial owner of a company shall be bound to provide the information required under sub-regulation (1) to the company without delay. Without prejudice to the aforesaid, the company shall obtain the information required under sub-regulation (1) from the shareholders of the company and, or from any natural person whom it has reasonable cause to believe to be a beneficial owner, who shall be bound to provide the said information to the company without delay, and every beneficial owner who acquires, disposes of, increases or reduces his beneficial interest in the company shall be bound to immediately provide the said information to the company. 

(3) +The information referred to in sub-regulation (1) shall be entered and held by the company in a beneficial owners register to be kept at the registered office of the company or at such other place in Malta as may be specified in the Memorandum or Articles of Association of the company.+ 

(4) The company shall not enter the name of a new shareholder or any changes to existing shareholdings in the register of members unless it has obtained, as may be applicable, information on the underlying beneficial ownership as required in accordance with sub-regulation (1) of this regulation. 

(5) If default is made in complying with the provisions of this regulation, the company and every officer, shareholder and beneficial owner of the company who is in default shall be jointly and severally liable to a penalty, and, for every day during which the default continues, to a further penalty: Provided that an officer of the company shall not be liable if he had exercised all due diligence to comply with the provisions of this regulation and the default was not due to any act or omission or negligence on his part.

(2) Where a notice of transfer or transmission of shares is delivered to the Registrar for registration in accordance with article 120(3) of the Act or where there is an increase or reduction of the issued share capital or a restructuring of a company’s share capital or changes in the voting rights, the company shall, together with the said notice or other documents as applicable, also deliver to the Registrar a notice in the form set out in the First Schedule to these regulations, indicating whether or not there has been a change in the beneficial ownership of the company and providing the information as required under sub-regulation (1) where applicable. 

(3) The Registrar shall not register a notice of transfer, transmission or allotment of shares or any other document relating to changes in issued share capital or voting rights unless the requirements of sub-regulation (2) have been complied with. 

(4) The notices of changes in beneficial ownership referred to in sub-regulations (1) and (2), duly completed, shall be signed by at least one director of the company or the company secretary and a certified true copy of the official identification document for every beneficial owner shall also be submitted to the Registrar.

Hey [~accountid:62ea2a7032850ea2a3243bf4] - thanks for raising this. I’ve created a legal ticket to set out our position on this issue 💪 

----

The key concern for Bolt is making sure that we are properly fulfilling our role of *matching passengers/customers with drivers who are willing to provide the service(s)*. It’s on Bolt to ensure that there aren’t mismatches, or we’ll be viewed poorly by passengers and drivers.

If Bolt is careless or takes liberties then this _could_ escalate reclassification risks, but common sense should see us steer well clear of that 👌 

{color:#4c9aff}+*(1) Transport Categories*+{color}{color:#4c9aff} {color}{color:#ff5630}*(*{color}{color:#ff5630}+*Emphasis: ‘Drivers Needing the Right Equipment’*+{color}{color:#ff5630}*)*{color}

* *Bolt Standard:* auto-enrolling all drivers into Bolt’s standard category is fine.
* *Premium / Luxury Categories*: auto-enrolling drivers into additional premium categories is fine, where all relevant requirements are met.
* +*Categories with specific customer requirements*+*:* we should only enrol drivers that can meet these requirements - we should not assume. For example:
** *only drivers with electric vehicles* should be entered into ‘+electric vehicle+’ categories.
** *only drivers with child seat(s)* should be entered into ‘+has a child seat+’ categories.

We can rely on a driver confirming this at sign-up / confirmations at regular intervals (as applicable). If we aren’t checking this in advance, then there is obvious scope for upset customers and public embarrassment.

The best way to avoid such situations is to make sure Bolt has the relevant information to hand well in advance of the launch of the category.

{color:#4c9aff}+*(2) Ancillary Services*+{color}{color:#4c9aff} {color}{color:#ff5630}*(*{color}{color:#ff5630}+*Emphasis: ‘Driver Preference / Choice'*+{color}{color:#ff5630}*)*{color}

Drivers sign-up to Bolt principally to provide passenger transportation services; they aren’t ‘handy-men’ agreeing to perform *_any_* type of work. 

To avoid causing major annoyance to drivers / passengers, we should ideally avoid ‘auto-enrolling’ drivers into ancillary services such as:

* *Bolt send* categories.
* *Pet transport categories:* where either:
** an owner wants to travel with his/her pet owner and there are no local rules that require drivers to accept this (note: accessibility laws may require drivers to offer transport for guide dogs).
** the pet is transported _without_ its owner... if this is a thing people actually want… (?!)

Again, we can rely on a driver confirming this at sign-up / confirmations at regular intervals (as applicable). 

The best way to avoid any difficulties is to get opt-ins sorted well in advance of the launch of the category.

But if we absolutely *_need_* to ‘auto-enrol’ drivers into ‘*Ancillary Services*’ categories (i.e. where this is commercially essential for a launch) then ideally: 

# We should make drivers fully aware of it in advance (15 days’ notice minimum), with multiple emails / in-app messages before launch explaining the service and how drivers can opt out. 
# We should make it +very clear+ what this type of work this is (in-app) before a driver accepts it. Hopefully, that is already the case.
# During initial launch periods, we should not hold it against drivers who refuse to accept this sort of work (i.e. Bolt should not apply ‘acceptance rate criteria’ from Day 1 of launch). Clearly, Bolt shouldn’t be blocking drivers for refusing work that they never agreed to perform, or were not properly informed of - there are obvious reclassification concerns with this.
# When drivers repeatedly refuse this work we should proactively ask if they want to opt out.
# +*Always*+: local counsel should be consulted (and a legal ticket raised to that effect) well in advance of the launch of the category to identify any other relevant strategies. If a market is particularly sensitive for reclassification reasons, it may be the case that local counsel recommends that that auto-enrolment is not appropriate, in which case this will need to be navigated on a ‘per-market’ basis.

Stating the obvious, we should only ‘auto-enrol’ for ancillary services if that is commercially absolutely necessary. If that is the case, points 1-5 should be addressed as a matter of course.

----

I trust that’s clear - if not let me know 👌

Hi [~accountid:712020:23c4a07a-5439-48b0-ad38-6e41f2c8a4a6] thanks for reaching out on this topic 💪 

In short, we need to collaborate on finding an alternative approach to ‘quizzes' as they will adversely affect the reclassification risk profile in all markets. 

The most relevant part for yourself is part (1) but I’ve also set out a re-cap on the difference between training and guidance (with examples etc.) for the benefit of other stakeholders that I’ve added to the ticket.

Let’s have a call on this with the other stakeholders to discuss next steps 🙏 

----

{color:#4c9aff}+*(1) Overview and Recommendations*+{color}

{color:#4c9aff}+(i) Summary of Issues:+{color}

Restricting access to work behind ‘passing a quiz’ is generally inappropriate in all markets because it is comparable to ‘*Employer-Like Training*’.

Bolt is already subject to reclassification claims that expressly mention that Bolt is ‘training’ drivers ‼️ 

For these reasons, mandatory quizzes should not be deployed in +*any*+ market without first:

* trying to identify an alternative solution that imposes less risk;
* in the event that an alternative cannot be found, there must be +compelling reasons+ that justify the approach.

Fortunately, there +ought+ to be alternative solutions available by issuing *‘Guidance’* in a timely manner that achieves the same result. 

{color:#4c9aff}+(ii) Proposed Alternative Solution:+ {color}

* Relevant Guidance can be provided in-app from time to time / via in app messaging.
* After a block, Guidance is provided to drivers in-app when they first log back into the platform:
** this is provided over several screens which must be clicked through;
** the tone of the Guidance is appropriate. 
* This approach would be workable in +*all*+ markets 🌍 

Input on this approach from all relevant stakeholders is sought and welcome 🙏

{color:#4c9aff}+(iii) Other Essential Info:+{color}

Going forwards all references to *‘Training’* in our internal and external documents must be avoided - this is inappropriate and creates significant risk for Bolt ‼️ 

----

{color:#4c9aff}+*(2) Understanding the Issues*+{color}

{color:#4c9aff}+(i) Background:+{color}

Bolt is an intermediary technology platform that enables service providers ("*SPs*") to connect with customers. SPs are either:

* independent and working for themselves ;
* working on behalf of their Fleet; 
* substitutes that work for an ISP

In all cases, SPs do +*not*+ work +*_for_*+ Bolt (as an employee)

{color:#4c9aff}+(ii) Independent Contractors and Employees: key differences+{color}

Independent contractors are generally expected to have the necessary expertise to perform their services. For example, when a plumber arrives at a house, the homeowner does not provide him with his tools, nor does the homeowner tell him how he should perform his services.

By contrast, employers are expected to issue training to their employees from time to time, as a means of controlling how they perform their work and ensure uniform standards are met.

To avoid escalating its reclassification risk profile, Bolt must at all times treat drivers as if they are acting as part of a separate business, rather than +_belonging_+ to Bolt’s business.

{color:#4c9aff}+(iii) The difference between ‘Guidance’ and ‘Training’:+{color}

For our purposes:

* *‘Guidance’* is offering suggestions on conduct whilst reserving an SP’s free will and autonomy. 
* *‘Employer-Like Training’* is providing mandatory instructions (‘do this, do not do this’).

Guidance can often achieve the same effect as training.

 Consider the following comments:

* {color:#ff5630}_“You cannot tell passengers rude jokes.”_{color}
* {color:#36b37e}_“Be mindful and respectful of passengers: different people may find different things offensive.”_ {color}
* {color:#36b37e}_“Please be aware that malicious or reckless behaviour that causes offence is prohibited by our platform terms.”_ {color}

Of these, only the first comment inappropriate because it is a command. However, the second and third comments are OK ✅

See the below Annexes for more examples of suitable and unsuitable wording.

{color:#4c9aff}+(iv) What can Bolt provide Guidance on?:+{color}

In short, anything. Obvious examples are:

* How the platform works ✅
* How to use the app ✅
* Behaviour that may be considered a breach of our terms (including matters relating to safety) ✅

so long as that doesn’t cross over into inappropriate activity. 

For comparison, a fast food chain employer might:

* give mandatory instructions over how its employees act and talk ❌
* give mandatory instructions over _exactly_ how food is prepared and served ❌
* require mandatory uniforms to make it clear that the employee ‘belongs’ to the fast food chain ❌

----

{color:#4c9aff}+*Annex 1: Examples of Suitable Wording*+{color}

+*_Guidance to help avoid negative interactions with passengers_*+

*_This guide is designed to help you avoid misunderstandings and ensure a safe and comfortable environment for everyone._*

+*_Everyone is different_*+

_Being different is wonderful! But it does mean we must avoid making assumptions about how people want to be talked to and interacted with._

_We recommended that you keep the following key topics in mind to avoid accidentally upsetting your passengers:_

* *_cultural differences_* _- what's tolerated in one culture may be very offensive to another._
* *_age differences_* _- some people may be particularly sensitive to feeling vulnerable because of their age._
* *_comment on appearances, relationship status, gender and sexual orientation_* _- these topics may be perceived as intrusive and rude, even if you are trying to be kind, so it’s important to be mindful to avoid overstepping any boundaries._
* *_personal space -_* _everyone has their own limits when it comes to personal space. Being aware of this will help you avoid unexpectedly upsetting a passenger._

+*_Problematic behaviour that might be considered harassment_*+

_Harassment covers a wide range of unwanted behaviours that may upset, humiliate or intimidate an individual. Nobody wants to be harassed. Bolt takes all occurrences of harassment very seriously and all reports of harassment are thoroughly investigated._ 

_Examples include:_ 

* _making offensive or hateful comments and/or jokes;_
* _unwanted touching or invasion of personal space;_
* _inappropriate images and gestures; and_
* _discrimination based on race, gender, religion, or similar._ 

_Such behaviour may even be considered a criminal offence._ 

_Bolt takes all occurrences of harassment very seriously and all reports of harassment are thoroughly investigated._ 

*_How you should respond to harassment:_*

* _If the situation is critical, you can use the “_*_Emergency Assist_*_” option in the app’s Safety Toolkit to call the local authorities, or you can call local authorities directly._
* _If there’s no immediate danger, you can report the incident by turning to our_ *_Customer Support_*_. You can also refer the matter to local authorities if you think this is appropriate._

*_When Bolt is notified that you may have harassed a passenger:_*

_In these circumstances we may be forced to take any of the following actions:_

* _your access to the Bolt platform may be suspended pending an investigation into your conduct;_
* _your access to the Bolt platform may be terminated in entirety;_ 
* _we may share our findings with authorities;_ 
* _any other actions which are appropriate in the circumstances._

_We encourage you to fully cooperate with us so that we can best determine the appropriate action._

----

Please remember I’m only talking about ride invoices here.

However, the company is subject to 18% VAT. So, in their monthly invoice we reflect this 4.53 once again VAT inclusive, except this time VAT is 18%.

Using the following query I found a lot of orders (where a change destination happens) where the riders pays way more than she should (route-estimation is not used apparently for orders with a change destination). Waiting on the Pricing team response: [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CGLJZE1SA/p1712662976537539|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CGLJZE1SA/p1712662976537539|smart-link] 

{noformat}with two_prices as (
    select
        p1.created,
        p2.order_id,
        p2.city_id,
        p1.change_reason,
        p1.predicted_price as p1_price,
        p2.predicted_price as p2_price,
        p1.distance as p1_distance,
        p2.distance as p2_distance,
        p2.distance - p1.distance as distance_diff_m,
        p1.type,
        p2.type,
        p2.created,
        p2.change_reason
    from glue.ng_public.pricing_order_prediction p2
             INNER JOIN glue.ng_public.pricing_order_prediction p1 ON (
        p1.order_id = p2.order_id
        )
    where p2.created_date = date '2024-04-08'
      and p1.created_date = date '2024-04-08'
      and p2.change_reason = 'client_destination_changed'
      and p1.change_reason is null
      and p2.distance - p1.distance > 2000
    order by p2.order_id, p2.created
)
select
    est.created,
    tp.order_id,
    tp.city_id,
    tp.p1_price,
    tp.p2_price,
    tp.p1_distance,
    tp.p2_distance,
    est.output_route_distance_m,
    est.output_route_confidence,
    cot.ride_distance,
    cot.ride_price,
    cot.price_review_status,
    cot.price_review_comment,
    cot.price_review_reason
from two_prices tp
INNER JOIN glue.tracking.route_estimation_get_route_estimation est ON (est.input_order_id = tp.order_id and est.input_city_id = tp.city_id)
INNER JOIN glue.ng_public.company_order_try cot on (cot.order_id = tp.order_id and cot.city_id = tp.city_id)
where est.created_hour between timestamp '2024-04-08 00:00:00' and timestamp '2024-04-08 23:59:59'
    and cot.created_date = date '2024-04-08'
    and est.input_trip_leg = 1
    and est.input_partial_result is null
    and tp.p2_distance - est.output_route_distance_m > 2000
    and cot.ride_price = tp.p2_price
    and est.output_route_distance_m > 0
    and est.output_route_confidence > 0.9
    and est.input_city_id = 325
order by est.created {noformat}

I previously wanted to ask only about the possibility, that’s the reason I didn’t provide additional details. 

*The idea:*

* We have 9 different teams (mechanics, fleet, customer support etc) that are working under the summarised working time regime and they provide us data with the excel spreadsheets. Spreadsheets are constructed and structured very differently and the principles of data provision also vary between them, so there are special apart rules of data processing for each of these 9 schedules. 
* Each month we manually add working hours (incl night hours, overtime hours, public holiday hours) for our scheduled workers from 9 different excel files to the payroll system Merit. Additionally to that we are manually comparing absences we have in Workday and in the spreadsheets, because quite often the data don’t match. 
* We would like to automate this process so that each Team Lead would add working hours of their scheduled employees directly to Workday (or another time tracking tool) and then from Workday (or from another time tracking tool) those working hours would automatically fly over to our payroll system Merit (with the API).
* The goal is to streamline and automate the process of tracking and integrating employee working hours from various teams into the payroll system. 

*The reasons we need time tracking tool:*

# *Efficiency* - The streamlined workflow will enhance overall efficiency, allowing payroll analysts to save working time and focus on more strategic tasks. This solution will reduce manual work and enhances workflow efficiency. *Our opinion is that our organisation needs such a solution to be ready to accommodate with potential future growth*. If we are planning to grow or for example take drivers under the payroll then we must have already tool that is working properly and allows us to manage higher headcount and track their working hours. 
# *To reduce manual work and save time* - Automating the data transfer process will significantly reduce the time spent on manual data entry and verification. Each month it takes about 1.5 working days of time to manually add hours from excel files to Merit. In case Payroll Analyst notices mistakes in the schedules, it can take all together up to 2 or 2.5 working days to communicate and wait answers from all the parties (employees, team leads, WD team) to fix discrepancies between schedules, Workday and Merit. _Besides quite often Payroll Analyst notices that there are some absences in the schedules, which are not registered in Workday (for example employee just forgets to register his annual leave or personal day in Workday, though this absence is marked in the schedule). And it takes precious working time:_
## _to contact those employees and ask them urgently add absences to Workday_
## _to contact their managers and ask them to urgently confirm these absences_
## _in case it’s too late (new month begins) to contact Workday team in order they could add correct data to Workday_
## _to do final control of the made changes from Payroll team side_
# *Totally we can save here up to 2 working days of working time for Payroll Analysts only (of course it depends on the amount of mistakes and questions)*.
# *Changes in the summarised working time periods* - Due to changes in EU regulations from 2024 related employee work and rest time we have to change the summarised working time periods from 1 month to 3 (or 2) months. That change will cause additional manual calculations on the Excel spreadsheets that are not easy to manage for the Team Leads. We already have one team that is working based on 3 months summarised working time and unfortunately there are mistakes monthly. We are not ready for that change without having a automated solution. The idea is that we can set-up the system in a way that summarised calculations are made by the system. 
# *Approvals* - The idea is that each Team Lead has to approve the monthly hours in the system before Payroll team receives the data and starts processing the payroll. Having “approval” will discipline the Team Leads to provide us the data on time and to check the data in more detail before giving the approval. 
# *To reduce mistakes coming from the manual data entry* - And of course automated things will anyway reduce the mistake percentage. 



If setting up time tracking in Workday is not possible then I think we have to search for another solution from the outside.

Discussed main issues (on spend caps and country-level decisions) with Avi and Nastya

Brought up some solutions:

[https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dvwiKOxYqpsohomInQYBJgQr0QCboh6WEytqTG6GBvo/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dvwiKOxYqpsohomInQYBJgQr0QCboh6WEytqTG6GBvo/edit|smart-link] 



*Potential solution description*

h4. The problem of spend caps
Additional formulas were required to make sure that the spend that the curves are suggesting are possible.

The structure of suggested dashboard (link above) can support importing budgets from the spreadsheets.
But I suggest we do *not incorporate it to any dashboards*, because it will make the process *slower* (if changes are done in spreadsheet, you will need to update fivetran, then the data mart)

Instead, I suggest that we make a *spreadsheet template* that will import spend cap for each channel and have the formulas that return the cap in case model suggestion is above it


h4. The problem of country level spends
It seems that we actually have *two separate issues* (budget distribution issue and measurement issue) that are related to the types of campaigns we have. Let’s have a look at those by types of campaigns that we have.

*Type 1:* Campaign targets only one main city. 
* *No issues*.
* Business decisions are city level. Campaign is regulated by budget also on city level

*Type 2:* Campaign targets one secondary city or multiple secondary cities.
* *Budget distribution issue* (No specific measurement has been carried out, but we need to distribute budgets)
* *Possible solution:* make curves based on attribution for a city (set of cities) that is(are) in campaign _(just like we do for main cities that do not have models yet)_

*Type 3:* Campaign targets the whole country (due to limited targeting opportunities)
* *Measurement Issue* (we assume that whole budget goes to main city)
* *Possible solution:*
** Understand how much it actually is an issue (check share of budgets going to the main city). 
** If is an issue, we might go for country-level measurements

h5. Why country-level curves might not be as good?
* Country-level curves would *require country-level experiments*. Seems that often we would have to sacrifice city-level experiments for them
* *Experiments* on country-level might require *larger budgets* (due to potentially larger noise)
* Country-level curves in general might be *less accurate* (more noise coming from multiple cities, launches and their differences)
* *MOST IMPORTANTLY,* Country-level curves are good at providing answers to LMMs, but do not give direct answer on *how to split budgets between campaigns* to Ads team (which they will have to do anyway).
*We could have the following situation:*
* We make country-level curve
* We approve budgets on country-level
* (We can even exclude some main cities)
* Ads Team takes country-level budgets and sees the following in business manager:
** Campaign 1: Warsaw,
** Campaign 2: Krakow
** Campaign 3: Gdansk
** Campaign 4: Rest of Tier2
** Campaign 5: Tier3
* Ads team will need to split budget among those. And to achieve it, Ads team will most probably do it *proportionally to population or GMV (which is what we wanted to avoid)*
